What Is the Four-Lesson Cycle?
A Repeating Instructional Architecture
The Jurassic English™ curriculum organises ALL literary study around 
the Four-Lesson Cycle — applied to every core text across all five 
levels.
This ensures the full Thinking Cycle™ is completed for every piece of 
literature studied.
The Thinking Cycle™
Analyze Evaluate
Justify Reflect
The cycle is not a formula — it is a scaffold. Teachers 
adapt activities, prompts, and CEIW structures to the age, 
CEFR level, and textual complexity at their tier. The 
architecture remains constant; the intellectual demand 
scales.
SAMPLE
·
jurassicenglish.com/products

The Four-Lesson Cycle at a 
Glance
Excavation — Analyze
Deconstruct vocabulary, surface narrative, and text architecture. 
Students become fossil-hunters: 
what is buried in the language?
Strata — Evaluate
Assess character motives, moral dilemmas, and competing 
interpretations. Students examine the 
geological layers of 
meaning.
The Justification — Justify
Construct a formal CEIW argument anchored in text evidence. 
Students build the warrant — the logical bridge between claim 
and evidence.
The Impact — Reflect
Connect the text to self, society, and the ecological world. 
Students consider the 
living consequence of the fossil record.

1. Syllabus by level
Level
1
—
Foundation
Field Detail
Typical age 5–7
CEFR Pre-A1 / A1
Purpose First stories, ﬁrst thinking. Children hear and read real
picture books, learn calm attention, and say their ﬁrst
claims aloud and on paper.
Outcomes (1) Retell a known story in order; (2) give a one-sentence
claim with "because"; (3) take part in the lesson routine
calmly.
Unit themes Family, school, weather, animals, daily routines, identity,
local stories
Skills Listening, oral retell, phonemic awareness, sentence-level
reading, drawing and speaking
CEIW depth Claim only (spoken or one written sentence)
Portfolio 1 retelling and 1 claim card per text; 1 audio recording per
term
Assessment Bands (Emerging / Developing / Secure / Advanced) on
Claim
Promise to parents Your child reads real stories, produces their ﬁrst thinking,
and grows conﬁdent taking part.
Exit Retells a known story; gives a one-sentence claim with
"because"; takes part calmly in the routine
Level
2
—
Development
(Early
Reasoner)
Field Detail
Typical age 7–9
CEFR A1+ / A2
Purpose From stories to evidence. Children move from telling what
happened to citing the text to support what they think.
Outcomes (1) Write Claim + Evidence paragraphs (3–5 sentences)
citing the text; (2) retell aloud with at least one reference to
the text; (3) use the full lesson routine with support.
Unit themes Community, fairness, choices, belonging, environments
Skills Past simple, connectives, describing words, opinion
phrases, reading short real texts

Field Detail
CEIW depth Claim + Evidence
Portfolio Evidence notebook: 4 short paragraphs and 1 spoken retell
with evidence per term
Assessment Bands on Claim and Evidence
Promise to parents Your child learns to support every idea with evidence from
the text — a habit, not a test trick.
Exit Writes a coherent CE paragraph; cites one piece of
evidence aloud; uses the full routine
Level
3
—
Expansion
(Developing
Analyst)
Field Detail
Typical age 10–12
CEFR A2+ / B1
Purpose From opinion to interpretation. Children learn to add
meaning, not just repeat the evidence — the most
important move in the programme.
Outcomes (1) Write a CEI response where the interpretation adds
meaning; (2) defend an interpretation aloud with evidence;
(3) use hedging accurately (may, might, suggests, perhaps).
Unit themes Citizenship, sustainability, choice and consequence,
perspective
Skills Modal verbs, hedging, reporting verbs, interpretive
vocabulary, reading longer texts
CEIW depth Claim + Evidence + Interpretation
Portfolio Interpretation folder: 2 multi-paragraph CEI responses, 1
paired-text response and 1 spoken piece per term
Assessment Bands on Claim, Evidence, Interpretation
Promise to parents Your child learns to say what the evidence means, not just
what it says.
Exit CEI response with real interpretation; oral defence with one
piece of evidence; accurate hedging
Level
4
—
Mastery
(Academic
Builder)
Field Detail
Typical age 13–15
CEFR B1+ / B2
